texts.preamble: Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Kabc020121112021 In The Court Of The Iv Addl. Small Causes And Addl. Mact., Bangalore, (Scch-6) Present: Smt. Chetana S.F. B.A., L.L.B., Iv Addl., Small Cause Judge & Acjm, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 7th Day Of November 2024 M.V.C.No.1834 Of 2021 Santosh Kumar Pandey S/o Ramachandra Pandey Aged about 38 years
texts.facts: The petitioner's case in brief as follows: On 23-2-2021 at about 8.30 a.m. when the petitioner was riding his splender pro motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-53-EJ- 9918 on New BEL road, near H.P. Petrol bunk, Bengaluru from north to south direction i.e., from Kuvempu circle side towards Ramaiah junction, at that time, driver of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371 came from his behind at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle to its right side, as a result petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and motor cycle was also damaged badly. It is further stated that petitioner took treatment at hospital as inpatient and spent money for treatment. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, working as Interior wood work supervisor at Gopalan Enterprises and getting salary of Rs.25000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, he is permanently disabled and lost his income. Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents. 3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte and respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement. 4. Respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that the policy particular mentioned in petition OG- 18-1701-1831-00000153 is issued to vehicle No.DL-1-RY-4747 from 8-5-2017 to 7-5-2018 only and this does not cover date of accident that is 23-2-2021 and no policy is issued to the offending vehicle at the time of accident. The policy coverage details mentioned in the petition are false and fabricated and not issued by this respondent. The owner of the vehicle has not submitted the claim form and other documents like RC,DL, permit etc., for verification. On the date of accident, offending vehicle was not holding effective DL which is in contravention of the conditions and MV Act. The offending vehicle was having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply in the public place, in this regard jurisdictional police have fled charge sheet u/s 66 and 192 of MV Act and there is a violation of provisions of MV Act. The petitioner has suppressed the true fact and colluded with the first respondent and jurisdictional police and filed false case against the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371. The petitioner was not wearing safety head gear at the Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/ 2 time of alleged accident. Hence pays to dismiss the petition. The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and in his support P.W.2 to 4 are examined. The respondent No.2 got examined one Jayanth Inamadar-Manager legal in respondent No.2 company as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1 to Ex-R3. 7. In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 95 documents as Ex- P1 to 95 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, notice under col.133, reply to notice, IMV report, charge sheet, ordersheet in CC No.1647/21, wound certificate, discharge summary, record showing treatment at Multispeciality hospital, medical prescriptions, medical bills, aadhaar card, pan card, DL, form No.6, x-rays, advance medical bills. 10.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the respondent No.2 has taken the contention that the autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD- 5371 is not at all involved in the accident and same is implicated in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to the second respondent. And all the police records are manipulated. The evidence on records shows that after lodging of the complaint by petitioner, Sadashivanagar traffic police have registered FIR as per Ex-P1 against the Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/ 3 driver of the offending vehicle autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371. Though counsel for the respondent No.2 argued that there was a delay of one day, but MLC produced Ex-P86 clearly shows that petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 23-2- 2021 soon after the accident at 1 p.m. and the history of the injuries is clearly mentioned as history of RTA near BEL road on 23-2-2021 at 8.30 a.m. and he was rider of the two wheeler and was hit by the autorickhaw. Ex-P86 and 87 MLC clearly shows that there was an accident between two wheeler of the petitioner and autorickshaw and involvement of the vehicle. 13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied." Consequently, I hold Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/ 4 that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-03-AD-5371. 15. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656. Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation. Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343. In support of their contention, respondent No.2 got examined Jayanth Inamdar- Legal Manager as RW-1 who in his deposition has testified that the insurance policy Santhosh Kumar Pandey vs Lakshmi on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110808401/ 8 No.OG-18-1701-1831-00000153 as stated in the claim petition is not at all issued to the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AD-5371 and the insurance policy details mentioned in the claim petition are disclosing that it is a fake, fabricated one and there was no contract of insurance between 1st respondent and 2nd respondent as on the date of alleged accident.
